properties.name: design_regions did not return in 300 s on a freshly started server, twice, and left the shared daemon needing --stop-shared
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-09-11 while exercising all 180 served tools. `design_regions` is the one tool in the surface that could not be made to return.

Its own description bills it as the cheapest possible orientation read: *"What parts this design has, so a session that holds NOTHING can pick where to stand. The one orientation read that asks for no seed, no scope and no topic — call it at check-in, before you have a lane."*

TWO ATTEMPTS, BOTH ON THE LIVE GRAPH (4,131 nodes / 24,140 edges), debug binary:
  1. Default arguments — still running at 180 s. That attempt was killed by MY OWN restart of the shared server mid-sweep, so it proves only ">180 s" and the failure is not attributable to the tool.
  2. `depth: 1` on a FRESHLY STARTED server, nothing else in flight — the shared server accepted the request and **did not answer within 300 s**, then reported itself possibly wedged; `reflow2-mcp --graph-path <graph> --stop-shared` cleared it.

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT COVERED BY THE EXISTING LATENCY WORK. `fact:the-agent-surface-profiled-orientation-is-35-of-40-seconds-and-two-causes-are-located` profiled the TEN tools an agent actually drives, taken from real session usage. `design_regions` is not among them — which is consistent with it being new enough, or slow enough, that nobody drives it. So the four located causes there say nothing about this, and this is a separate observation rather than another instance of them.

⚠️ WHAT `depth` SHOULD HAVE DONE. The parameter's own documentation says depth 1 is the CHEAP setting and explains the choice with measured numbers — *"at 3 … all 56 Components cover 595–903 nodes … At 1 the same parts cover 17–139 nodes"*. Passing 1 did not help, so whatever dominates is not the per-part walk the parameter controls.

🛑 BOUNDS, and they matter. This is a DEBUG binary; `fact:every-cost-number-today-was-a-debug-build-and-the-live-store-is-7x-its-content` measures the profile alone at 2.2x on `loop_status`, so a release build would be faster — but 2.2x does not rescue a >300 s call, and no release measurement was taken. The machine was also under memory pressure during part of the sweep. NOT MEASURED: where the time goes, whether it terminates at all, or whether it is superlinear in nodes, edges or Components. No profiling was done inside the call and the root-cause skill was not run.
properties.value: {"attempts":2,"outcome":"no return","first_attempt_s":">180 then killed by my own server restart","second_attempt_s":">300 on a fresh server","server_state_after":"wedged; cleared with --stop-shared","depth_tried":1,"build":"debug","graph":"live, 4131 nodes / 24140 edges"}
